hints: Use conservation of mass to write the mass of B as $y=50-x$.
Translate 'rate of increase of A is proportional to the mass of B' as $dx/dt=ky$ and substitute for $y$.
walkthrough:
Use conservation of mass: the total mass of compounds $A$ and $B$ is constant and equal to $50$ throughout the reaction:
$$x + y = 50 \implies y = 50 - x$$

Translate the physical rate law: the rate of increase of mass of $A$, $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}$, is directly proportional to the mass of $B$ present at that time, $y$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} \propto y \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = ky$$

Substitute $y = 50 - x$ into the proportionality relation:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = k(50 - x)$$

hints: Separate the equation from part (i) as $dx/(50-x)=kdt$ and integrate.
Use $x=0$ at $t=0$ to determine the first constant, then use $x=25$ at $t=10$ to find $k$ exactly in terms of $\ln2$.
Exponentiate and isolate $x$ as a function of $t$.
walkthrough:
Separate the variables $x$ and $t$ in $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = k(50 - x)$:
$$\dfrac{1}{50 - x}\,\mathrm{d}x = k\,\mathrm{d}t$$

Integrate both sides with respect to their variables:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{50 - x}\,\mathrm{d}x = \int k\,\mathrm{d}t$$
$$-\ln(50 - x) = kt + c$$

Apply the initial condition $x = 0$ when $t = 0$ to find $c$:
$$-\ln(50 - 0) = k(0) + c \implies c = -\ln 50$$

Substitute $c = -\ln 50$ back into the solution:
$$-\ln(50 - x) = kt - \ln 50$$
$$\ln 50 - \ln(50 - x) = kt \implies \ln\left(\dfrac{50}{50 - x}\right) = kt$$

Use the second given condition $x = 25$ when $t = 10$ to evaluate the constant $k$:
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{50}{50 - 25}\right) = k(10)$$
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{50}{25}\right) = 10k \implies \ln 2 = 10k \implies k = \dfrac{1}{10}\ln 2 \approx 0.069315$$

Substitute $k = \dfrac{1}{10}\ln 2$ into the logarithmic equation:
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{50}{50 - x}\right) = \dfrac{t}{10}\ln 2 = \ln\left(2^{t/10}\right)$$

Exponentiate both sides with base $e$ to remove the natural logarithm:
$$\dfrac{50}{50 - x} = 2^{t/10} \quad \left(\text{or } \mathrm{e}^{0.0693t}\right)$$

Take reciprocals and solve explicitly for $x$ in terms of $t$:
$$\dfrac{50 - x}{50} = 2^{-t/10} \quad \left(\text{or } \mathrm{e}^{-0.0693t}\right)$$
$$50 - x = 50\cdot 2^{-t/10} \implies x = 50\left(1 - 2^{-t/10}\right) \quad \left(\text{or } x = 50\left(1 - \mathrm{e}^{-0.0693t}\right)\right)$$
